newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES UP ON HOT WEATHER, CHICAGO.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES UP ON HOT WEATHER, CHICAGO.

text.p: Most Hungarian grains futures went limit-up due to continued hot and dry weather and a Chicago price rise, Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) traders said on Tuesday.
They added that the market was cautious about forecasts of rain over the weekend.
"We do pay attention to weather forecasts... and prices will certainly start falling as the rain does," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
Hungary's Meteorological Office forecasts at least five milllimeters of rainfall next weekend over 70 percent of the country.
In the meantime, the May average temperature remains 3.3 degrees above the 30-year average, it said.
Maize futures rose the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all maturities, with July finishing at 19,920 forints, December at 21,600 and May at 23,300.
Milling wheat prices went limit-up for July, August, September and March, October and December put on 280 forints to end at 25,430 and 26,060 forints and January rose 300 forints to 26,300.
Traders said rising Chicago prices added extra upward pressure on the Hungarian market.
"Wheat rose five to six cents per bushel, maize two to three cents," Szolyka said.
Budapest feed wheat and barley futures took their cue from milling wheat as barley went limit-up for all termins and feed wheat put on 280 to 400 forints.
Sunflower seed remained flat and virtually tradeless with five lots changing hands.
Total grains turnover of was modest, at 488.3 million forints, but still more than triple Friday's 153.7 million.
Milling wheat accounted for 602 lots of the 1,009 lots traded.
